key_concepts: The heart is a hollow muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body.
The heart has upper chambers called atria and lower chambers called ventricles.
The left and right sides of the heart are separated by a muscular wall called the septum.
Valves in the heart keep blood flowing in one direction.

Blood has four main components: plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.
Plasma is the liquid part of blood and transports blood cells throughout the body.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to body cells and contain hemoglobin.
White blood cells fight infection by producing antibodies and acting as phagocytes.
Platelets help stop bleeding by forming clots.
Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart and have thick elastic walls.
Veins carry deoxygenated blood back to the heart and contain valves to prevent backflow.
